title: Front Brake Disc Shield — SVT Performance Package
introduction:
This shield procedure applies to the 5.2L Mustang with the SVT Performance Package. A little shield has quite an entourage: the wheel, caliper and brake disc must come out of its way first. I keep the whole return journey in view, because supporting the caliper and reinstalling the wheel correctly matter just as much as the shield bolts.

Use this guide with the linked brake-disc, wheel-and-tire and lifting references. Their illustrations explain the access sequence, and their installation details remain part of this job. Read the separately attributed EPA home-mechanic dust-control preparation below before starting.

items.name: Match the brake package
items.detail: Use the [Brake Disc — Vehicles With: SVT Performance Package](#/document/G1716189) procedure for this job. It requires removing the wheel and tire through the [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) procedure. Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189), [Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693183) and [Wheel and Tire Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693193) before starting.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around or underneath the vehicle. Otherwise, a remote start could cause personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person starting the engine during service; an accidental start can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect yourself and handle chemicals safely
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts; failure to do so can cause serious personal injury. Read the material safety information sheet before using the specified cleaner or lubricant. Improper chemical use can cause serious personal injury. Keep solvents away from ignition sources because they may ignite or explode, causing serious personal injury.

items.name: Control brake dust
items.detail: Do not breathe friction-component dust or blow it from components or storage containers with compressed air. Remove dust using government-approved techniques. The dust may present cancer and lung-disease hazards and can irritate the skin, eyes and respiratory tract, cause allergic reactions or contribute to other chronic effects. Seek medical attention or advice if irritation persists. Failure to observe these precautions can cause serious personal injury. An approved cleanup method must be identified before dusty friction components are disturbed.

items.name: Gather equipment and replacement fasteners
items.detail: Have suitable lifting equipment, a caliper-support hook as illustrated in the brake-disc reference, a wire brush and torque equipment for the different fasteners involved. The [Brake Disc reference](#/document/G1716189) specifies Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner — VOC Compliant / Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner (PM-4-A, PM-4-B). The [Wheel and Tire reference](#/document/G1686507) specifies Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant (XL-2). Have new caliper mounting bolts ready: the removed caliper bolts must be discarded. The new caliper bolts are tightened to 136 lb.ft (185 Nm) during reassembly.

items.name: Position the vehicle on a suitable hoist
items.detail: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on a hoist using [Jacking and Lifting — Overview](#/document/G1663631). Verify that hoist capacity covers the vehicle, cargo and modifications. Locate the triangles stamped into the body or frame and use the illustrated lifting points and arm positions. Lifting elsewhere can let the vehicle shift or fall, causing serious personal injury. Incorrect hoist positioning can cause unintended vehicle movement, serious personal injury or death. Do not use the engine to power the drive wheels unless all drive wheels are elevated.

items.name: Check lift clearances
items.detail: Position hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering-linkage components to prevent damage. Before using a drive-on lift, check for underbody interference. On a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped; also protect the axle and rear cover from contact.

items.name: Observe jack restrictions
items.detail: If a jack is used during handling, its capacity must cover the vehicle, cargo and modifications. Work on a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block wheels remaining on the ground. Support the raised vehicle with floor stands; never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack, which could lower unexpectedly. Unintended movement can cause serious personal injury or death. The supplied emergency jack is only for changing a deflated tire, not this repair. Never jack against either bumper; the covers will be damaged.

items.name: Remove the wheel safely
items.detail: Remove the wheel nuts and wheel-and-tire assembly as shown in the linked procedure. Never use heat to release a seized wheel nut; it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. If a wheel is cracked, deflate its tire before removing the wheel from the vehicle; failure to do so can cause serious personal injury. Do not weld or peen a wheel needing repair: install a new wheel, because attempted repairs can lead to wheel failure and serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect the caliper and disc
items.detail: Remove the caliper mounting bolts, discard them, and position the caliper and brake pads aside. Support the caliper with the illustrated hook rather than letting it hang from its brake hose; hanging it can damage the hose. Handle the brake disc carefully when removing it from the hub.

items.name: Prepare the disc and wheel mounting surfaces
items.detail: As part of disc refitting, clean the brake-disc mating surfaces with a wire brush and the cleaner specified in the linked brake-disc reference. Before installing the wheel, remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel and hub or brake-disc mounting surfaces. Secure any rotor-to-hub fasteners so they cannot interfere with those surfaces. Otherwise, the wheel nuts may loosen and the wheel may come off while driving, causing loss of control, serious injury or death.

items.name: Keep anti-seize confined to the pilot
items.detail: Apply a thin coat of the specified anti-seize only between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot, as highlighted in the wheel illustration. Keep it off the wheel-to-disc mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces; contamination can damage components. I use the highlighted pilot ring as the boundary, not as an invitation to coat everything nearby.

items.name: Finish wheel installation
items.detail: Position the wheel and install its nuts finger tight initially. With the vehicle resting on its tires, tighten the nuts in the illustrated star/cross pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). This specification requires clean, dry stud and nut threads. Skipping the star/cross pattern can produce high brake-disc runout and accelerate roughness, shudder and vibration.

items.name: Check operation and arrange the wheel-nut recheck
items.detail: Apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake-system operation, as required by the brake-disc procedure. Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling the wheel. Wheels can loosen after initial tightening; missing this recheck can result in serious injury to occupants.

items.name: Home-garage preparation
items.detail: Do not judge asbestos content by appearance. EPA suggests professional servicing when the material is uncertain. If that is not possible and professional dust-control equipment is unavailable, its home-mechanic guidance describes wet wiping: use a low-pressure fine mist of water or detergent-amended water to wet the brake parts, then wipe them with a cloth. Keep bystanders, food and drinks away.

items.name: Contain dust and waste
items.detail: Do not blow dust with compressed air or clean it with a dry rag, brush or garden hose. Do not use an ordinary vacuum lacking HEPA filtration. Keep contaminated clothing and dust out of the house; change clothes and wash soiled clothing separately. EPA recommends double-bagging asbestos waste and following local disposal rules. Read the full [EPA brake-and-clutch guidance](https://www.epa.gov/asbestos/current-best-practices-preventing-asbestos-exposure-among-brake-and-clutch-repair-0) before starting.

items.name: Keep the instructions distinct
items.detail: This is EPA guidance for home mechanics, not a claim that every brake contains asbestos or that employer OSHA duties apply to your home garage. Ford’s later wire-brush instruction concerns mating-face preparation; it does not replace dust control.

items.name: Maintain vehicle restraint
items.detail: Keep the parking brake applied during this front-disc-shield work.

items.name: Before lowering for final wheel tightening
items.detail: After the removed caliper and other components removed for access are fully refitted, make sure the parking brake is applied before lowering the vehicle. Restore ground-wheel restraints as the tires meet the ground, before final wheel-nut tightening.

edits.text: NOTE: Installation details also appear in the removal steps. Read both sections before starting.
edits.why: The tightening specification beside a removal action is needed when the part goes back on.

edits.text: Remove the brake disc to expose the shield. Refer to: [Brake Disc - Vehicles With: SVT Performance Package](#/document/G1716189) (206-03 Front Disc Brake, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: After completing the lifting preparation, remove the wheel nuts and wheel. Support the caliper with a hook, remove and discard its mounting bolts, and position the caliper and brake pads aside without loading the brake hose. Then remove the disc from the hub. Keep the caliper supported throughout; letting it hang from the hose can damage the hose.

edits.text: Remove the highlighted mounting bolts, then remove the brake disc shield. On installation, tighten the shield bolts to 106 lb.in (12 Nm).
edits.why: I use the blue shield and magenta fasteners in the illustration to distinguish this hardware from the nearby hub and suspension parts. The tightening value is an inch-pound specification, so select the torque equipment and units accordingly.

edits.text: Install by reversing removal: refit the shield and its bolts, then reinstall the brake disc, caliper and brake pads, and wheel-and-tire assembly through the referenced procedures.
edits.why: Reversing the order also brings back the linked installation requirements: clean the disc mating surfaces, use new caliper mounting bolts, prepare the wheel mounting faces, confine anti-seize to the pilot interface and finish wheel tightening with the vehicle on its tires. Complete the brake-pedal operation check and the required later wheel-nut recheck. The last bolt going tight is not the end of this job.

changes.before: The linked access sequence starts with the wheel and tire, then moves the caliper and brake pads aside before the disc comes off the hub. Its drawing shows the caliper supported by a hook and marks its mounting bolts for disposal. Keeping that weight off the brake hose prevents hose damage; simply leaving the caliper dangling is not an acceptable shortcut.

Keep the caliper supported throughout; letting it hang from the hose can damage the hose.
